_comment: MOCK fixture for the epoch fence (contract/generation-fence.v1.md). It states the CASES and their EXPECTED outcomes so a future C++ test can assert them. NOTHING here has been run against the binary; this round changed source and fixtures only.
_schema_note: not a manifest — it is a list of {applied_generation, manifest_generation, expect} rows a test drives build_plan with

cases.name: no generation has been applied yet
cases.why: -1 is «nothing applied», so the very first manifest is never stale

cases.name: the same generation re-planned
cases.why: equal is NOT stale: a Core that restarted and re-reads the manifest it already applied must still be able to plan it

cases.name: a manifest restored from a backup
cases.why: THE BLOCKER THIS FIXES. Before the fence this row planned and acted exactly as if it were current. ok stays true because this is a plan that declines, not the absence of a plan; the refusal is about the DOCUMENT, so its scope is empty; and there must be ZERO actions.

cases.name: a manifest far in the past
cases.why: a stale checkout of the very first manifest

invariants_a_test_must_hold: a STALE_GENERATION plan carries ZERO actions — not «the unchanged ones», not «the ones that differ»
the refusal's `scope` is empty: it is about the document, not about a service
`plan.ok` is true, so a caller can tell a reviewed refusal from a malformed plan
the fence is checked BEFORE ordering and before any per-service rule, so a stale document cannot produce a cycle refusal or an owner refusal instead — the reader is told the one thing that matters
not_yet_true: PlanInput.applied_generation is not persisted by the resident loop, so the fence is INERT in production today
the fence has not been compiled, and these cases have not been run
the persistence must be written only AFTER a generation is carried out, or a crash between plan and action advances the fence past work that never happened
